sources.title: The Met: The Eastern Mediterranean and Syria, 2000 to 1000 B.C.
sources.note: Museum chronology, Overview and Key Events: Middle Bronze reurbanization, fortification and exchange; later Egyptian hegemony. Its older claim about alphabetic writing only at the end of the Late Bronze Age is not adopted. Atlas geometry is independently decoded in identities.json and geometry-checks.json.

sources.title: Moshe Kochavi: Canaanite Aphek (1978)
sources.note: Excavator report, opening historical sketch, Middle Bronze paragraph only. Later thirteenth-century buildings and lexical tablets are outside this map window and not used. Biblical synchronisms are not adopted.

sources.title: Israel Nature and Parks Authority: Tel Dan, Station 8, the Abraham Gate
sources.note: Official multilingual site guide: Canaanite gate, arches, chambers, earthwork and rapid blocking. English says approximately 4,000 years; Arabic dates around 1800 BCE. Biblical identification and global superlatives excluded.

sources.title: Koh, Yasur-Landau and Cline: Characterizing a Middle Bronze Palatial Wine Cellar from Tel Kabri (2014)
sources.note: Original open research, Introduction, Materials and Methods, Results and Discussion. Forty jars found; only 32 sampled for this analysis. Botanical additives are interpretations, not all securely identified ingredients. Use revised Kabri abandonment chronology from Lazar 2020 rather than the older 1600 BCE date.

sources.title: Melissa Cradic: Residential Burial and Social Memory in the Middle Bronze Age Levant, ASOR 2017 abstract
sources.note: Printed page 98, PDF page 98, Building 12/K/15 at Megiddo. Excavation researcher reports 10 to 15 residents, at least 45 burials over about 150 years, varied funerary treatments. Family interpretation based on mortality profile, not genetic proof.

sources.title: Scott and colleagues: Exotic foods reveal contact between South Asia and the Near East during the second millennium BCE (2020)
sources.note: PNAS original, Table 1 and Results: Megiddo MGD 011 and MGD 018 only. Indexed full original Results read; direct PMC fetch encountered challenge. Table independently checked through indexed University of Valencia repository mirror (handle 10550/76877, 142350.pdf). Do not use the much later Tel Erani banana evidence for this interval. DOI 10.1073/pnas.2014956117; repository mirrors grouped as one work.

sources.title: Michael C. Carlos Museum: Loom Weight, Jericho, 1955.122 B
sources.note: Original museum indexed catalogue: excavated Jericho, Middle Bronze, 2000 to 1600 BCE, clay. Label describes surviving textile tools/fragments, draped robes and kilts with toggle pins and rarer sewn tunics. Some fiber and loom reconstructions are explicitly hypothetical. Direct HTML extraction contains no label; indexed original checked.

sources.title: Vainstub and colleagues: A Canaanite’s Wish to Eradicate Lice on an Inscribed Ivory Comb from Lachish (2022)
sources.note: Jerusalem Journal of Archaeology 2, pages 76 to 119. Full original PDF text read. Pages 80 to 83: secondary pit, teeth and louse membrane; page 90: transcription and translation; pages 102 to 103: proposed 1700 to 1550 BCE paleographic dating and unsuccessful radiocarbon. Roman scholarly transcription used, no invented ancient font.

sources.title: Bob Becking: The Power of an Inscription (2023)
sources.note: Original Journal of Northwest Semitic Languages abstract, volume 49 number 2. Disputes ḥṭ as tusk and proposes inscription. Only this stated interpretive disagreement is used; full article not inspected.

sources.title: Lazar and colleagues: Earthquake damage as a catalyst to abandonment of a Middle Bronze Age settlement, Tel Kabri (2020)
sources.note: Original paper, Abstract, Tel Kabri section and Discussion: revised high chronology around 1700 BCE, rapid collapse, nine possible earthquake effects and proposed seismic explanation. Do not generalize to all Canaan or treat absence of weapons as definitive proof.

proposedOverrides.name: Canaan
proposedOverrides.summary: Bronze Age city-states and communities of the southern Levant.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Distinct regional-context card. Exact missing indexed record, no aliases. Related modern Israel record is not a historical identity equivalent.
batchIdentityNotes.map: Single historical-basemaps polygon, 2000 to 1500 BCE, bounds 34.035 to 36.767 E and 29.941 to 34.312 N. All six featured excavation sites are inside; Byblos inside, Ugarit outside. Public opening distinguishes outline from city territories.
batchIdentityNotes.continuity: Regional end date is not a cultural extinction or one conquest; no successor links asserted.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Lachish ivory comb scholarly Roman transcription and editors’ English translation; proposed date range and secondary find context explicit. Alternative ḥṭ reading cited separately. No fabricated ancient glyphs.
batchIdentityNotes.sourceLimits: Specific household and diet samples are not universal customs. No invented hospital, school system, sewer or toilet claim. Textile reconstructions remain qualified; lice-comb is actual personal-care evidence. Kabri updated chronology replaces older 1600 BCE dating.
